name: Variance-aware blends: pythagorean lerp, orbit, RMS, cosine, cubic
plain: bleh has blends that handle variance loss on purpose. Pythagorean lerp rescales weights so squares sum to 1 at the default, the right correction for independent inputs. Orbit moves on a quarter circle so endpoints are a and b. RMS interpolates in a power domain. Cosine and cubic only reshape t and do not correct variance.
math:
pythagorean: raw=(|1−t|^p+|t|^p)^(1/p), p=2; mag=raw^growth_power (default 0→1, optional soft clamp); w=(1−t,t)·mag/raw
orbit: a·cos(tπ/2)+b·sin(tπ/2)
rms: (lerp(a^p,b^p,t))^(1/p), sign from blended or chosen input, p=2
cosinterp: ((a+b)−(a−b)cos(πt))/2
cuberp: a+(b−a)(3t²−2t³)
weighted_average: (a+t·b)/(1+|t|)
label: from code
surprise: growth_power default 0 makes mag=1, so pythagorean_lerp defaults to true variance preservation for independent inputs; orbit has no denominator, so it matches that shape without an eigen-check.
